issues.legal_issue: A reference to acquisition law in a scheme statute does not incorporate that law where the scheme statute leaves acquisition to the general law and merely modifies specified provisions.
material_facts: The scheme statute did not itself provide for acquisition of land for the scheme, but left acquisition to the general acquisition law.
The scheme statute referred to specified provisions of the general acquisition law and modified some of them for the scheme.
The case disclosed no contrary intention that the general acquisition law should be applied only as it stood when the scheme statute was enacted.
issues.conclusion: The general acquisition law applied as it stood at the relevant time of acquisition; its later amendments were not excluded by incorporation into the scheme statute.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a reference in one statute to another is by incorporation or merely by reference depends on the language and relevant circumstances. When a statute is incorporated by reference, a later amendment to the incorporated statute does not affect the receiving statute. But where acquisition is left to the general law and specified provisions are merely referred to and modified, the general law applies as it stands at the relevant time, absent a contrary intention. The Court relied on Mahindra and Mahindra Ltd. v. Union of India and Another, [1979] 2 SCR 1038, and Secretary of State for India in Council v. Hindustan Co-operative Insurance Society Ltd., [1958] IA 259 at 267.

rule.if: acquisition_proceeding and acquisition_uses_general_law and referenced_rules_are_locally_modified and contrary_intention_absent

predicates.acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns acquisition of land for a scheme.
predicates.acquisition_uses_general_law: The scheme framework leaves the acquisition of land to the generally applicable acquisition law.
predicates.referenced_rules_are_locally_modified: The scheme framework refers to specified acquisition rules and modifies some of them for the scheme.
predicates.contrary_intention_absent: The governing framework contains no contrary intention that the general acquisition law is fixed to its version at the time the scheme framework was enacted.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition proceeding for a scheme uses the general acquisition law, the scheme framework only locally modifies referenced rules, and no contrary intention appears, the general law as it stands at the relevant time applies.

issues.legal_issue: A scheme-approval notification must be published within the applicable time limit measured from the first publication of the scheme notice that serves as the acquisition notification.
material_facts: The scheme notice was first published in a newspaper on May 30, 1977.
The notification approving the scheme was published on June 30, 1980.
The first publication of the scheme notice had the same effect as publication of the acquisition notification, and the applicable law required the approval notification within three years.
issues.conclusion: The approval notification was published beyond the permitted period, the scheme notice lapsed, and the acquisition proceedings lapsed; the approval notification was invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 36 and 42 and clause 2(1) of the Schedule to the Punjab Town Improvement Act, 1922, the first publication of a scheme notice under section 36 is substituted for and has the same effect as publication of a notification under section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. The first proviso to section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act required the declaration to be made within three years. The approval notification therefore had to be published within that period from the first publication of the scheme notice; once the period expired, the notice lapsed and no further action could be taken under it.

predicates.scheme_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns land acquisition for a scheme under a scheme-improvement framework.
predicates.scheme_notice_serves_as_acquisition_trig: The first public publication of the scheme notice is treated as the event that starts the acquisition timetable.
predicates.approval_notice_published_after_applicab: The notification approving the scheme was published after the applicable time limit measured from the first publication of the scheme notice.

issues.definition: When a scheme-acquisition proceeding uses the first scheme notice publication as its acquisition-timetable trigger and the approval notification is published after the applicable limit, the acquisition proceedings lapse.
